Energy data review

Energy action planning

Russell’s background includes more than 20 years of work across building energy, carbon and sustainability, including experience with museums, theatres, offices, factories, estates, heritage buildings, cultural venues and specialist facilities.

Name: Predict Golf
Description:
Our Methodology.
 
Phil Mickelson has come up short on the 9th at Pebble Beach. He faces a seemingly impossible up and down to make par. But to no one's surprise, he hits a miracle shot to within 3 feet and sinks the putt.
 
Why was this to no one's surprise? Because Phil is known as one of the best scramblers in the business. Of course knowing about Phil's strengths is one thing, but knowing about the strengths of every one of the 150 odd players in something like the AT&T is impossible.
 
Fortunately, through today's tracking technology, there is data on every shot, hit by every player, in every tour event. So in  our world, when we see Phil - or any other players - faced with that tough up and down, we look back at every other time in the last two years that he's hit a similar shot in similar conditions and forecast the probability of what happens next based on that prior experience.
 
In fact, we do this for every shot a player plays in a round, simulating a full round of golf for each player at  the course they are about to play. And then we do it again, and again, and again - around 10,000 times per player. We do this for every player, and for all four rounds if the player makes the cut. And then finally for every simulation, we figure out the winner, and over the course of 10,000 simulations assess how often each player wins to compute a 'modelled winning probability'. This probability represents a scientific value for the chances of each player winning. And if that scientific value is higher than the odds available in the sports betting markets then we have identified a money-making opportunity.

Three actions per signal — copy the message, snooze it, or mark it not relevant. That's the whole workflow. No new dashboard to babysit. No process for your reps to follow.

  • Deals you lost — a warm nudge when a cold account changes.

 And we only email you when something has actually happened — no empty digests, ever. We store company names only: no contact names, no personal data, so your GDPR surface stays small.

Scores are important to us, but it's what individuals make of them that matters most of all.

Name: Article 27 Representation
Description:
Article 27 Representation provides peace of mind to organisations controlling and processing data across borders between the UK and Europe; and the rest of the world. 
From our final departure from the EU the UK will become as a 'third country' for data privacy purposes, with no equivalence or adequacy guaranteed.
 
At the same time, the UK will have its own amended version of GDPR, enacted under the terms of The Data Protection, Privacy and Electronic Communications (Amendments etc) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019, making the EU will become a 'third country' to us for data protection purposes.

Organisations monitoring the behaviours of data subjects, or providing goods and services into the UK from Europe; or from Europe into the UK, that do not have a physical presence in the other jurisdiction will need to have representation in line with Article 27 of the General Data Protection Regulations. Failure to do so will expose UK organisations to fines of up to the greater of 2% of global turnover, or €10m; whilst European and other 'third country' organisations will be open to similar sized fines for non-compliance within the UK. 
But the impact of Brexit doesn't stop there: in the event of a data breach, organisations who are headquartered in one of the jurisdictions, but are also collecting, controlling and/or processing personal data of subjects in the other could find themselves exposed to investigation and fines from regulators in BOTH the EU and the UK; doubling the maximum fines to the equivalent of 8% or global turnover or €40m! 
To mitigate this risk Article 27 Representation provides a presence in both jurisdictions, allowing organisations to continue to operate with minimal disruption and peace of mind in knowing that not only are you complying with both sets of regulations, but that you have someone there to represent your organisation’s interests. 
For more information about how we can help contact: enquiries@article27representation.co.uk

In the 1990s, when a person was diagnosed with NPD they were told they would never meet anyone else affected, as the conditions are so rare. But people directly impacted by the disease – patients themselves, their family members and friends – began setting up support groups, connecting families and drawing in impassioned and dedicated people to fight their corner, determined that no family diagnosed with NPD should face the future alone.

Today, we have an international network of non-profit groups, supporting hundreds of families, and we continue to grow. By joining together through the INPDA, we give Niemann Pick Diseases a stronger global voice, and progress towards effective treatments for these conditions is accelerated.

Have you ever stopped to think about what you’ve learnt and the steps you’ve taken to get there? 

From completing college to joining your dream company, starting your own business to reaching retirement, all those mini skills and lessons learned are an integral part of who you are. Yet, many people under appreciate the effort they have put in to the achieving goals or the obstacles they've overcome.

We hope by doing this, it will encourage greater flexible working, provide full or part time income, enable greater movement of people into areas they are passionate about and improve the health and wellbeing of people by removing perceived fears or barriers to success. 

The world is changing so fast, new industries are born, skills shortages are apparent, traditional businesses closing down or adapting, incomes reducing.  We all need support. With the prediction that 50% of the worlds workforce will become freelancers by 2020 there is a need for a platform that flexs to your needs, not the other way round. And with the continuing improvement of AI, it will be people, not technology that will help those affected. 

Our goal is for iKnow to speed up the ability for people to progress. In time we plan to become an intelligent platform that understands all the steps our community has made in each of their respective fields. This will allow any man, woman or child to search iKnow and get a personalised career plan. By detailing everything that is required (courses, companies, mentors and roles), we can direct them to you, the amazing people that can help them make that change and hopefully make the world a better place.

Description:
Windmills is a registered charity that provides direct specialist bereavement care and support for children and young people who are, or will be, facing the death of a loved-one, or someone very close.

This might be the sudden, often unexpected death of a sibling, parent, or friend, or due to a limited-life diagnosis due to a terminal illness. 

Facing the reality or news of the death of such a loved one can be deeply traumatic and disorientating for the surviving child. Often the response is a cauldron of confusions and emotions; anger, disbelief, guilt, anguish, withdrawal, detachment and numbing fears for all that is yet to come. Without expert and trusted care and support, such responses can irrevocably scar and derail a young person’s life and outlook and negatively shape their relationships, not only with death itself, but with life and living, themselves, their family, and their friends and the wider community.

Windmills’ specialist acute bereavement nurses work one-to-one with the bereaved child and their family and helps them turn the anger, trauma and negativity around,  shaping death’s sudden arrival into a positive, managed and contained acceptance of death’s inevitability and the building of sustaining and fulfilling fond memory mementos. Death is a reality we all face and which cannot be avoided, and for young people in Windmills care it can be resolutely faced, its emotions controlled and managed, and its impact greatly appeased.

Windmills’ nurses will often be the first ones to share with the child the news about the death, or its imminence. The nurses provide a caring, empathetic and expert support to the child and will help guide them through all the confusions and emotions that news of a loved-ones death will inevitably bring.

As industry experts we felt there was a better way to improve transparency on opaque financial products, helping to improve levels of understanding and better identify areas of risk.

The AssetQ management team have worked in the financial services industry and have over 100 years experience working with financial institutions, exchanges, fund managers and wealth firms.

Worse, many of the workplace training companies have no legally qualified staff to ensure that correct, current and legally accurate information is disseminated. This has led to companies being misinformed about their legal obligations and responsibilities when dealing with the D/deaf.
Being found guilty of discrimination is a costly business in more than just financial terms. Most people know what 'regular' disability discrimination looks like but would you recognise Deaf Discrimination if you saw it? With our help you can recognise it and prevent it. Reduce your risk and raise your profile as a Deaf Friendly organisation.
There are many examples in our lives of 'gathered information' and knowledge' that somehow just 'arrives' in our brains because we have absorbed it almost unintentionally. Legal Compliance to prevent Deaf-Discrimination is NOT the kind of knowledge that lands on your head... you have to actively seek it out - but once you know, it will change your life and how you think forever. 
You'll be a Deaf Champion and (we think) one more 'better' human out in the world that's able to do the right thing, say the right words, bang the right drum, and be on the right side of history.

Description:
Listen Limited is a secure, low cost, self-service platform that enables managers to quickly and effectively measure the mood of their team – highlighting potentially hidden issues and attrition risk that can then be addressed individually with team members.

Listen Limited requires no complex integration with HR systems, and your staff will instantly understand how to respond to our simple feedback process without training or confusion.

Using simple questions to your team, we compile a valuable summary report which shows which team members are unhappy with their current work situation, without revealing their individual responses.

Within a few minutes, you can start letting your staff know you care about their welfare and morale without expensive consultants, platform licensing or complex integration into your company systems.

Once your staff have responded to our intuitive and simple questions, we provide you with a valuable “Mood Analytics” report, for as little as 99p/c per person, giving informative insight into individual mood and morale.

Our platform does not ask difficult or detailed personal questions or attempt to store sensitive data around commercial topics like compensation. We keep our questions safe and high level so your HR department will be relaxed, and your staff will feel at ease.

Our service is entirely FREE for workers in public healthcare, education and emergency services. Please ensure you select the correct industry when registering to receive free reports.

Description:
SourceWise is an AI-powered information and verification platform for UK government and regulatory information.

Unlike conventional generative AI tools, SourceWise is designed around a verification-first architecture. 

Our system does not rely on probabilistic answers or unsourced text generation. Instead, it retrieves and cross-checks information directly against official UK government, regulator, and statutory sources.

Each verification is recorded through a dedicated audit and integrity layer, with verification events anchored using the Hedera Consensus Service. This creates an immutable, time-stamped record of when and how information was verified, providing transparency, traceability, and accountability that standard AI systems do not offer.

SourceWise is built for environments where accuracy and trust matter including employment, housing, healthcare, compliance, and public-sector decision-making  and where unverified or hallucinated AI output presents real risk.

SourceWise is not a legal advice service. It is an information and verification platform designed to help users access, understand, and validate UK rules and guidance using official sources, with a clear audit trail.

XMap is a behaviour-first experience mapping system for pharmaceutical and healthcare brands. It maps the full lived experience of a disease, condition or treatment pathway - and shows brand teams where the market is being shaped, before the prescription is written.

A behavioural planning layer that connects experience, evidence, decisions and system constraints to clear brand direction:
• Clinical segments and behaviour-led personas
• A structured, source-linked evidence store
• Interactive XMap with XMap AI
• Priority unmet needs and intervention points
• Executive summary and localisation options

WHY IT MATTERS.
XMap helps brand teams enter the journey earlier, focus on the three or four unmet needs that disproportionately shape outcomes, and build positioning, messaging and activation from evidence rather than assumption. It informs over 65% of a strategic brand plan - and stays a living, queryable asset across the lifecycle.

TRUSTED ACROSS PHARMA
Applied across more than 25 disease areas - from cardiovascular and immunology to oncology, rare disease, renal, respiratory and vaccines - by global, regional and local teams.

Built for pharmaceutical governance
Hosted on Microsoft Azure (UK and EU). ISO/IEC 27001 inherited. Aligned to UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018. AI used selectively, under strict governance - every insight source-linked, confidence-rated and human-validated.

XMapTM is a product of Uservox.

Analysis of Risk Register

Staff Training & Awareness Sessions

Name: RippleXn
Description:
What is this https://github.com/octree-labs/octree


The GitHub repo you sent —
 https://github.com/octree-labs/octree — is an open-source AI LaTeX editor, essentially a modern alternative to Overleaf for writing technical papers, research documents, and mathematical content. 

What Octree (the project) actually is

Octree is a tool for writing and editing LaTeX documents with AI assistance.

LaTeX is the formatting language used by:

academics

scientists

mathematicians

engineers

research labs

to write things like:

research papers

technical reports

equations-heavy documents

academic theses

The Octree project tries to make that easier by combining:

a LaTeX editor

AI writing assistance

document tooling like TikZ diagrams, BibTeX references, and equation editing. 

In simple terms:

Octree = AI-powered Overleaf replacement.

What’s actually inside the repo

From the repo structure and related repos, it includes things like:

AI-assisted text editing for LaTeX

tools for math equation conversion (image → LaTeX)

templates for academic writing

a deployable web interface (often deployable on Vercel) 

So developers can:

self-host it

extend it

build tools for research writing

Why people build tools like this

Academic workflows are painful:

ProblemOctree tries to solveLaTeX is powerful but hardAI helps generate/edit LaTeXOverleaf is SaaS onlyopen-source alternativeMath typing is slowimage → equation conversionCitation management messyintegrated BibTeX tools

Important: the name “Octree”

The name Octree comes from a computer-science concept:

An octree is a data structure that splits 3-D space into eight parts recursively (like a cube subdividing into smaller cubes). 

But in this project it’s mostly just a brand name, not necessarily the core algorithm.

Would this be useful for you?

Probably not directly for RippleXn, because it’s focused on academic document writing, not:

intelligence pipelines

vector search

timelines

signal ingestion

Description:
FloodList

About Our Work

We report on all the major flood events from around the world. By doing so, we aim to raise awareness of the risks of flooding and the devastation caused by the increasing number and severity of flood events.

Our news reports and articles help people understand more about floods, what can be done to prepare, protect, stay safe and recover.

FloodList include articles on flood-related issues such as warning systems, mitigation and control, flood recovery, flood damage repair and restoration, as well as flood insurance. Our reports and articles also include information about the extraordinary humanitarian, aid and relief efforts that need to be made in the aftermath of so many flood disasters.

We are in regular contact with those who have suffered from flooding, and those who are concerned about the threat of flooding and understand their concerns (some of us have suffered from flooding ourselves).

We want our readers to understand how a changing climate and a changing world is increasing the threat of flooding and hope to inspire helpful discussion and collaboration in preparing for and dealing with the effects of flooding.

Flood Disaster Risk Reduction
People across the world need to understand how to reduce the risk of flooding and build resilience. With this in mind, our reporting stresses the importance of disaster risk and recovery (DRR).

We believe the work of UNISDR and the Hyogo / Sendai Framework for Action demonstrates the way ahead for those threatened by floods.

Our Outlook is Global
Between 1995 and 2015, as many as 157,000 people died as a result of flooding. During that time, at least 2.3 billion people were affected by floods. Threats from sea level rises and increased rainfall, sprawling urbanization and widespread deforestation mean that many countries around the world now experience severe flooding on a regular basis. This is not limited to any particular continent or region. Nor is our reporting.

Scrubnet also publishes practical guidance covering technical SEO, web development, AI search, structured publishing and crawler behaviour. The aim is to turn hands-on experience, experiments and observable evidence into information practitioners can apply to their own work.

The Scrubnet Crawler Observatory is the research layer behind part of this work. It publishes machine-readable feeds compiled from authorised public content and records verified crawler requests through live access logs. This makes it possible to examine discovery, recrawling, content freshness, request formats and the technical conditions surrounding crawler access.

Authorised websites can join the observatory for free, helping broaden the sectors, site structures and publishing patterns represented in the dataset. A crawler request demonstrates access, not indexing, ranking, preference, AI citation or subsequent use. Findings are presented as descriptive observations rather than evidence of causation.

Scrubnet is practitioner-built, independent and evidence-led: a place for better tools, clearer technical knowledge and a more observable web.

Name: Proven EA: From fragmented guidance to assured decisions
Description:
Proven EA helps regulated organisations prevent governance failures caused by broken, fragmented guidance.

Since 2014, we have worked with boards and executive teams across defence, healthcare, housing, financial services and other regulated environments where policy, assurance and accountability genuinely matter. Our work has focused on helping management teams address complex operational problems where governance and guidance must function reliably under real-world pressure, including how organisations design governance, apply guidance in practice, and demonstrate assurance under scrutiny.

Across sectors, we observed the same recurring problems: critical guidance spread across disconnected documents and systems, unclear ownership, inconsistent application, and assurance processes that focus on document existence rather than usability or authority.

Sapience emerged directly from this experience. It is a secure, governed knowledge platform designed to make authoritative guidance usable at the point of decision, while strengthening ownership, auditability and regulatory assurance. The platform reflects patterns identified through real regulatory findings, operational failures and board-level decision-making — not abstract “knowledge management” theory.

Sapience is backed by more than a decade of board-level governance work in regulated environments, including direct exposure to regulatory findings, assurance failures and real operational risk.

Proven EA remains deliberately small and senior-led. We work closely with clients where context matters, applying hard-won experience of regulated environments to ensure governance, guidance and assurance arrangements stand up in practice - not just on paper.

Name: meeting.toolchest.org
Description:
Remote meetings are a lot easier to get right than many people realise. People use remote meetings because of their convenience, but by taking a different approach remote meetings can actually be more effective and engaging than most physical meetings. 

The internet provides different opportunities for collaboration, and these tools can be used to better achieve our meeting objectives. We should stop seeing remote meetings as a ‘pale reflection of the real thing’ and start seeing their potential to rectify what has become a source of inefficiency and frustration in many organisations. 

But not everything has to change at once, and there are many good practices we can take from physical meetings to ensure we get the best out of remote meetings. Adopting some of the practices below will help you to improve immediately and set you on a path to creating meetings which fully reflect your leadership. 

There are six areas to explore in thinking about making your remote meetings more effective:
•	Assembly - Having the right people, in the right place, at the right time, ready
•	Alignment - Agreeing a clear purpose and the practical steps to get there
•	Activity - Using the potential of the internet to engage full participation
•	Attention - Facilitating practices which help listening and understanding
•	Action - Building ownership of outcomes and actions to ensure progress
•	Assessment - Learning from experience and observation to improve further

Meeting Toolchest is a free online resource which has been created to support and promote all of the above - meetings which inspire and empower people to transform their organisations and themselves. It provides ideas, guidance, tools, and resources to support a simple step-by-step path to improvement that is open to everybody who runs and attends meetings. 

To get started, simply go to https://meeting.toolchest.org set yourself up a free account, and then follow your nose.

Voice-Clouds is especially relevant when the client is unable to reliably, or consistently, articulate what their needs or views might be to others. 

Voice-Clouds is about delivering a fulfilled and happy life. It is not about systems or processes. This means it is not affected by any change of government or an overhaul of services. The information it identifies will always be relevant. Having said that, Voice-clouds is perfect for addressing and simplifying the new ways of assessing and working that will result from the inevitable change required when the Children and Families Bill and the Care and Support Bill in England, and similar reform taking place in Wales are finalised in 2014. 

Voice-Clouds reflects the hopes or aspirations of the client and includes details of the sort of things that can make a difference to their day. It identifies their strengths and the things they enjoy doing most. It also acknowledges what's already working and explores ways to make that happen more. When necessary it explains how the world makes sense to them, enabling those around them to gain some insight into how they might be feeling or what they might want to do. It also includes how they can begin or continue to take their place in their community and society. 

Having this information makes it possible for providers and supporters to better enable the client, to lead as fulfilling and meaningful life with dignity as they are able.

Name: Cowgate
Description:
The Cowgate is a low-lying strip South of Old Town and running parallel with the Royal Mile in Scotland’s capital. The Cowgate is often considered to be part of Southside.

Edinburgh’s Cowgate today has become a popular pub and club area and even on the brightest sunny day can be a shadowy, dank place with its narrow road hemmed in by tall, dark tenements on either side.

Early history

The Cowgate's name is recorded from 1428, in various spellings, as Cowgate and in 1498 as Via Vaccarum.
It is derived from the medieval practice of herding cattle down the street on market days; a number of other streets in the old town of Edinburgh (such as Grassmarket and Lawnmarket) also reflect their market roots.

Describing the street in the 1581 edition of their atlas of major cities Civitates orbis terrarum, Georg Braun and Frans Hogenberg said the Cow Gate was where "... The noble families and city councillors have their residences, together with other princely houses and palaces most handsome to behold."

Gate is a Scots language word for "way" or "road", a cognate of similar words in other Germanic languages (compare with gait).

    Quality Studies - these vary from the traditional quality as accuracy style of study to a more modern holistic approach where fitness for purpose of the whole system is considered.

    New System Design - a major part of our work is assisting organisations in planning for and converting data from legacy to modern systems and providing a data centric input into the design of these new systems.

    Data Cleansing - either as part of an ETL (Extract, Transform and Load) process with a new system or as a housekeeping activity. We profile data sets, determine whether there is any need to intervene and if required make the necessary interventions.

Description:
SMcP Digital Ltd are document and records management B2B service bureau, based in the central belt of Scotland.

Our heritage dates back to 1972, when TR McPherson Microfilm Services was one of Scotland's largest document management, print and archive storage providers.

We specialise in working with organisations (Private, Public and Third Sector) to not only digitise their paper and microfilm records, but to release the data held within those records.

Paper (documents, large format drawings / plans and bound books) storage not only takes up space within the office, but is unproductive when searching for information. Storage systems can be costly to manage and are fragile to water damage. Security of paper records can be challenging to maintain. Locating misfiled documents / records is common practice in paper archives.

Microfilm was once the must have document management system for virtually every organisation, large and small. Microfilm is fragile to becoming damaged if not stored correctly. The equipment used to view microfilm formats is  expensive and becoming harder to find parts for aging equipment.

In todays modern world, we require access to data quickly. We require to work from any where and at any time. 

Scanning of documents, drawings and microfilm ensures the information held within these vital business records is suitable for modern working practices. 

Digitisation of historical paper records, saves space, reduce costs, improves productivity and ensures agile working practices.

Data extraction of the scans is vital for modern electronic document and records management systems.

We have fantastic working relationships with service bureaus throughout the UK to ensure a competitive and unbiased approach to managing your data.

Contact our team today to discuss how we can assist your organisation with not only capturing and scanning your archive filing systems, but extracting the information held within using modern AI driven systems and technology.

Description:
Recognising Misdiagnosis Between ME and Fibromyalgia Matters

At Hope 4 ME & Fibro Northern Ireland, we understand that many patients initially diagnosed with fibromyalgia may later receive a diagnosis of Myalgic Encephalomyelitis (ME). 
The overlap in symptoms—particularly chronic pain, fatigue, and cognitive dysfunction—often leads to confusion. Yet the hallmark feature of ME, post-exertional malaise (PEM), is too often missed or misunderstood.

By acknowledging this diagnostic journey, we:
 Promote accurate diagnosis and appropriate care
 Support patients who may feel overlooked or mislabelled
 Educate clinicians on critical distinctions
 Strengthen our advocacy for better training and services

We believe inclusion matters—and recognising misdiagnoses is key to delivering the support and awareness both ME and fibromyalgia communities deserve.

Name: Commissioner for Survivors of Institutional Childhood Abuse
Description:
The Commissioner for Survivors of Institutional Childhood Abuse promotes the interests of victims and survivors who were abused as children in residential institutions in Northern Ireland between 1922 and 1995.  

The Office of the Commissioner provides information to victims and survivors, raises awareness of their rights and entitlements and advocates for lifelong access to vital supports and services. 

The role of the Commissioner for Survivors of Institutional Child Abuse was a recommendation of the Historical Institutional Abuse Inquiry and is set out in the Historical Institutional Abuse (Northern Ireland) Act 2019, which provides the Commissioner with statutory powers:  

- To undertake or commission research into matters concerning the interests of victims and survivors
- To compile information concerning the interests of victims and survivors
- To provide advice or information on matters concerning the interests of victims and survivors
- To make representations or recommendations concerning the interests of victims and survivors

One of the Commissioner’s key responsibilities is to encourage the provision and coordination of relevant services to victims and survivors in Northern Ireland, including consideration of current levels of provision and identification of gaps.

Since its creation in 2020, the Office has engaged with over 1,200 victims and survivors. One in five people contacting the Office are survivors of child abuse outside its current remit.

Name: Albasoft Ltd
Description:
Albasoft is a health informatics company located in Inverness, Scotland

Since our inception in 1997 and incorporation in 2002 Albasoft has built a reputation for providing “Trusted Third Party” TTP services to the health and associated sectors.

In todays challenging Big Data environment transferring sensitive information between organisations can be a complex procedure particularly where exposure to related information can conflict with organisations governance and confidentiality procedures.

In many cases the information required is embedded in large legacy databases and cannot be extracted simply without exposing sometimes highly sensitive information to the receiving party and possibly breaching the data protection act.

The resolution is to appoint a trusted third party with both the technical skills and secure environment to extract the information and act as an “honest broker” between both parties to ensure that only the approved information is transferred.

The basic requirements of a TTP is that it must have no interest in the information it processes, either directly or through related activities. This ensures that exposure to sensitive information is minimised and both the organisation and individuals confidentiality is respected.

Albasoft have extensive experience in data mining and consolidating information from multiple diverse systems, particularly in a complex clinical and pharmaceutical records environment

Name: The Democracy Box
Description:
What is the Democracy Box?

The Democracy Box aims to promote understanding of our UK democracy and achieve a shared basic level of understanding by the majority of the population. The Democracy Box began as an Clwstwr funded R&D project in 2020 and grew into 3 prototype solutions which are ready to upscale and a toolkit for co-creation. 

The three prototype solutions are
1. The Democracy Box public Information Campaign
2. The Democracy Box Creative Cascade for Schools
3. The Talking Shop

The Democracy Box is not only about or for young people.  The R&D began by working with young co-creators aged 16-26 from across Wales because they were supposedly the most disengaged (they're not). Now it is time to recruit co-creators from all disengaged communities, groups and demographics. For more information please see The Democracy Box report https://clwstwr.org.uk/beyond-ballot-box-report or email omidaze@outlook.com

The Democracy Box is about finding new creative ways to share The Democracy Box Story so that everyone can understand our UK democracy and can take part.

Our UK democracy needs all citizens to be informed, actively encouraged to get involved and to understand that it is their democratic right to challenge, question, protest, shape, critique, debate and influence our democracy all year round and not just at the ballot box.
